body_text: Er waren voor ondernemer René Boxman veel redenen om over te stappen op het online bestelsysteem Orderli , maar de feilloze koppeling met hun kassasysteem Lightspeed K-series was één van de belangrijkste. Mede daardoor hoeft hij tot wel vier man minder personeel in te zetten. Op drukke dagen waaien er wel duizend gasten aan bij Bosbrasserie In de Sluis. De dagzaak annex bezoekerscentrum in Nationaal Park De Maasduinen (Well, Noord-Limburg) heeft tweehonderd zitplaatsen, waarvan de helft op het terras aan het water. "Motorclubs, fietsers, Belgische en Duitse vakantiegangers van de nabijgelegen parken, gezinnen; we ontvangen hier allerlei type mensen", vertelt René Boxman, die samen met zijn vrouw Rianne sinds tien jaar de brasserie runt. Gasten komen hier voor koffie met vlaai, pannenkoeken, broodjes of een andere versnapering van de uitgebreide menukaart. HOGER NIVEAU Zoals het een echte ondernemer betaamt, is Boxman altijd bezig met de vraag hoe hij zijn zaak en service naar een hoger niveau kan tillen. Toen de eerste bestelapps met QR-code op de markt kwamen, was hij er dan ook als de kippen bij: "Voor het begin van de pandemie hadden we hier die mogelijkheid al. Maar eigenlijk was ik niet zo tevreden, onder andere over de koppeling tussen de bestelapp en ons kassasysteem Lightspeed K-series." Dus toen Boxman tijdens de lockdowns tijd over had, besloot hij zich te oriënteren op andere aanbieders. Orderli kwam als beste uit de bus: "De stabiliteit van de app, de duidelijke en overzichtelijke interface, een goede backoffice, en – zo weet ik inmiddels: een heel fijne ondersteuning. Eventuele mankementen worden meteen opgelost." Bosbrasserie In de Sluis KOPPELING APP EN KASSA Ook over de koppeling tussen het kassasysteem en de app is de ondernemer zeer te spreken: "Die sluiten perfect op elkaar aan. Dat is natuurlijk een voorwaarde voor het goed functioneren van de dienst, maar onze vorige online bestelapp stapelde bestellingen voor dezelfde tafel vaak niet goed. Daardoor klopten bonnen niet, kwamen orders niet door of stonden we juist twee keer met dezelfde bestelling aan tafel. Met Orderli gaat dat foutloos", aldus de ondernemer. Dankzij de feilloze werking van de bestelapp kan Boxman op een drukke dag met drie tot vier man minder personeel toe: "We hebben nu alleen runners op de vloer staan, en één gastheer of -vrouw. Ook onze gasten kunnen goed uit de voeten met de app: zo’n 95% bestelt inmiddels via de QR-code."

title: Identifying ambiguous and low quality vehicle listings with HuggingFace transformers
summary: Cars.com is an automotive marketplace that connects car buyers and sellers. With nearly 25 years under our belt, Cars.com has become…
body_text: Machine Learning Data Science Transformers NLP Hugging Face Identifying ambiguous and low quality vehicle listings with HuggingFace transformers Alexis Carpenter 10 min read · May 20, 2022 -- Press enter or click to view image in full size My latest car — 2021 Mazda CX-5 Source: Cars.com Cars.com is an automotive marketplace that connects car buyers and sellers. With nearly 25 years under our belt, Cars.com has become synonymous with car shopping and regularly ranks as №1 in our competitive set when it comes to brand awareness. Car dealers and private sellers are able to list their available vehicles with photos and include information about the vehicle’s features, history, pricing and more. Consumers use the marketplace to research, read millions of reviews, shop for cars and connect with sellers to set up test drives and, ultimately, make a purchase. Note: The terms dealer and seller are used interchangeably throughout the following post. Press enter or click to view image in full size 1. Example vehicle listing from Cars.com including vehicle photos, features, and seller provided description. However, what happens when consumer trust is broken due to a lack of transparency from sellers? For example, one of the primary complaints from car shopping consumers is that the price listed online is not indicative of the price on the lot — a practice that is not unique to Cars.com and largely affects the entire industry. This is due to various reasons, but primarily because the price listed does not include dealer-installed add-ons, dealership or document fees, or added warranties. Whatever the case, sometimes the online price isn’t telling the whole story. Ambiguous pricing practices not only degrade the Cars.com brand because it reduces the trust that consumers have in our platform, it further unduly penalizes dealers who are being transparent about their pricing practices and who are standing by their online list price. Finally, such ambiguous pricing tactics directly go against Cars.com terms and conditions. In this article, I will summarize how we, as a Data Science team, approached this problem with a machine learning product we built that utilizes NLP techniques to proactively identify vehicle listings and sellers that may be engaging in ambiguous pricing practices. Background When shopping for products online consumers have come to expect that the price listed is what they’ll pay. Hidden fees reflect poorly on the business and cause distrust between buyer and seller. While this is not true of the majority of Cars.com’s listings, there are the rare few that sneak past (or those who disregard) our terms and conditions. Here’s what this might look like on a marketplace: The seller lowers the main listing price of a vehicle and then includes pricing caveats in the seller’s note.A vehicle may be listed for $29,000 but this listed price may exclude a $1000 document fee, which is noted in the seller’s note, bringing the out-the-door price to the consumer to $30,000 (See Figures 1 and 2 for example seller’s note texts). There are two key sources of information with regards to understanding the context behind pricing: 1) seller’s note and 2) dealer review texts. Seller’s note texts include vehicle or seller information provided to Cars.com directly from the seller , whereas dealer review texts provide consumers a space where the consumer can discuss their experience with a particular dealership. We used various NLP techniques to develop a machine learning product to proactively identify problematic listings. This allows us to then reach out to those specific sellers and request that they make the required changes to improve consumer trust and transparency on our marketplace . Prior to this model, Cars.com had to manually flag problem listings or wait until a consumer complaint. Methodology Given the wealth of textual information provided in seller’s note and dealer review texts, we focus on these two texts as sources for untrustworthy or ambiguous seller signals. We utilize a multi-label text classification approach where our labels correspond to specific categories of ambiguous pricing (e.g. price does not include additional dealership fees or add ons vs. price includes all rebates or incentives that not everyone will qualify for) to classify texts that may belong to multiple categories or labels simultaneously. Below is an example of a single seller’s note text and dealer review text and the sentences that would be flagged for ambiguous pricing. The example seller’s note text would be flagged for 1) requiring financing with a specific party (Finance_CashOnly); 2) price excluding taxes and title (Taxes_Registration); 3) price excluding fees and dealer installed add-ons (Fees). The example dealer review text would be flagged for 1) price excluding fees (Fees). 2. Example Seller’s Note and Dealer Review texts with corresponding ambiguous pricing-related sentences flagged. Model: Here we fine-tune a DistilBERT HuggingFace transformer model, which is a distilled version of BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) for multi-label text classification on our custom dataset. BERT utilizes a transformer, which is an attention mechanism that learns relations between words (or sub-words) in a particular text. Further, rather than reading the text sequentially (e.g., left to right) like directional models, the transformer encoding reads the entire sequence of words at once. This allows BERT to learn the words based on their surrounding context. For sentence classification tasks (i.e., where our goal is to categorize a given text into X number of predefined labels), BERT models take a sentence or a sequence of words as the input. This input is segmented into token embeddings, segment embeddings and position embeddings. The combination of such embeddings is the final input to the BERT Encoder. Press enter or click to view image in full size 3. The sum of these three token, segment and position embeddings acts as the final input to BERT. Token embeddings add a [CLS] token at the start and a [SEP] token at the end of each sentence and words are subjected to a transformation to word pieces (e.g., playing → play + ##ing). Segment embeddings indicate which sentence a word belongs to and the positional embeddings indicate its position in the input. Figure from Devlin et al., 2018 . BERT takes each block of this input sequence and passes it through a self-attention mechanism and a feed-forward neural network before being passed to the next Transformer encoder. The attention mechanism essentially decides at each step of the input sequence which other parts of the sequence are important contexts for the given item or word. For example, for our use case the context around the word “marked” affects how we interpret this word’s meaning. That is, the price being marked or marked down should be interpreted differently compared to the leather seats being marked. BERT specifically is bidirectional, meaning that it takes into account the prior and subsequent words into account simultaneously. The output vectors here are our word embeddings. We can then use the pooled outputs and feed this into our classifier to get our label predictions. However, as previously mentioned, we chose to use DistilBERT in order to reduce training and iteration time with minimal impact to model performance. Specifically, distillation is a process by which we can shrink networks to a reasonable size whilst minimizing the drop in performance. With distillation we are training a small student model to essentially mimic a larger teacher model as closely as possible. The idea behind distillation is that once a large neural network has been trained, its full output can be approximated by using a smaller network. As such, distillation results in a smaller model that is faster to train while still retaining the majority of BERT’s language understanding capabilities. Price Extraction: The use case of this model is to flag specific vehicle listings or sellers who are engaging in ambiguous pricing, vehicle damage or bait and switch strategies. Additionally, if available we also aim to extract specific dollar amounts to support price adjustments based on pricing strategies (e.g., +$899 for the online price excludes an $899 dealership fee). The only input to the model is the text (either seller’s note or dealer review text) which is scored across 14 labels related to ambiguous pricing and vehicle quality. Flagging such ambiguous seller signals in text allows Cars.com to be proactive in contacting sellers and allowing them a window during which they can update their listings to comply with Cars.com terms and conditions. For repeat offenders (sellers that use ambiguity in their pricing), our review system (powered by DealerRater ) acts as a feedback loop and impacts a seller’s reputation on our marketplace. Challenges faced Data distribution: Many example texts included mentions of fees not being included in the price but very few contained organic mentions of fees being included in the price. Given this, initial attempts highlighted the need for additional data augmentation to our training set as texts highlighting that fees that were included in the online price were incorrectly flagged for ambiguous pricing. For example, we introduced custom negation and topic concatenation rules to ensure that our model is not flagging any text that merely mentions pricing, fees or cosmetics but only those texts that are indicative of ambiguous pricing and low vehicle quality and further to improve performance when multiple signals are present in a given text. Identifying the classes and labeled data: Prior to this model we had a rough definition as to what would constitute ambiguous pricing or a low quality vehicle listing. As an initial step, we created 14 specific labels with corresponding definitions in collaboration with the Fraud and Product teams at Cars.com to identify specific types of ambiguous pricing or vehicle quality issues (e.g., dealer fees not included in price vs. minor cosmetic damage, etc.). 4. Proportion of seller’s note texts flagged across the 14 labels related to ambiguous pricing and vehicle quality. Our “other_hedging” label was the most frequent given that it included instances where the dealer mentioned that the consumer should call to confirm availability, price or features, whereas labels related to a listing requiring a specific trade-in of a given value or down payment were less common. Get Alexis Carpenter’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Remember me for faster sign in Explainability: A key component of our model is its ability to not only flag texts for ambiguous pricing or vehicle quality issues, but also to provide the specific segment of text that resulted in the listing or dealer being flagged. That is, we provide our teams with A) listings and dealers that are flagged for ambiguous pricing or low quality listings and B) the specific text(s) segment that contributed to the text being flagged. Evaluation & Results We tracked the F1 score, precision and recall when building and evaluating new versions of the model. These metrics are calculated by running the model against a gold-standard dataset that the model has not seen. After multiple iterations, our model that gave the best F1 score was finalized and our best F1 score was at 0.97 across our 14 labels. Key Takeaways In this section, I briefly want to discuss several key takeaways that while not directly related to modeling decisions were integral to the success of the product. Crowdsourcing Label Alignment: Before creating and experimenting with the training set, we needed to understand what labels and definitions we could use to create the training set. Given this we iterated on several sets of labels and definitions and received feedback from our ML as a Service, Product and the Fraud teams. This allowed us to have a single set of labels and corresponding definitions that all teams were aligned on prior to creating the training set. Flexibility of the Model: Further, we tried to build the model with ample flexible parameters. Such flexibility saves significant time when evaluating results and allows for course correction immediately if necessary with less effort. For example, we originally decided to have 14 labels that texts could be scored for. However, later we may want to update these labels and/or definitions based on feedback from other Cars.com teams. Shifting the number of labels and the label names requires changing 2 lines of code, saving a lot of dev efforts and will allow us to rapidly update and/or experiment with the model as the business use case evolves. Combine Techniques: It was important for us to try and combine a couple of different text augmentation techniques together to create our training set. This methodological experimentation provided us with much better results than going with some standard text augmentation techniques like back-translation, etc. Together, typo-aware training methods using TextAttack, custom concatenation rules, and custom negation rules resulted in the best model performance. Iterative Approach: Finally, we aimed to have a model that can be retrained in an iterative fashion, taking feedback from Cars.com teams in order to fine-tune or refine our labels and their corresponding definitions. Thus, we are able to take in mislabeled data and apply our augmentation techniques in order to create an updated training set and retrain our model as needed. Next Steps There are several limitations of the current model that we plan to improve upon in the future: Hierarchical labels: We are not currently taking into account relationships among labels and we are ignoring the fact that the generalizing pricing label, for example, is inclusive of fees. A potential future direction would be to utilize a hierarchical approach to label creation and modeling, such that generalized ambiguous pricing, for example, is inclusive of fees, incentives, financing, down payments and undisclosed ambiguous pricing. Price adjustment improvement: Currently we use ad hoc regex rules (e.g., if we extract more than 5 unique price values, this likely indicates a list of options, so we should take the average of the values extracted) to determine how to handle cases where multiple price values are extracted. Future work should focus on a more nuanced approach taking into account the actual sentence structure and the context surrounding the extracted value rather than merely the number of extracted values in a given text. Conclusion In addition to making Cars.com a more trusted and transparent car shopping marketplace, we built a model that is able to: Flag texts that likely contain mentions of ambiguous pricing or vehicle damage affecting vehicle quality Extract the specific sentence that contributed to that text being flagged for increased explainability Extract the price adjustments if the text was flagged for ambiguous pricing in order to provide a more accurate vehicle price for consumers and other downstream Cars.com ML products Be updated flexibly and iteratively based on a feedback loop initiated by various Cars.com teams as needed Cars.com is currently hiring for several Data Science/ML Engineering positions so please check out our careers page if you are interested in learning more! References HuggingFace transformers (DistilBERT) BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter Typo-aware training methods TextAttack augmentation

title: Let’s Get Sweaty! Get In Shape For Summer With Boxing
summary: Getting in shape for summer doesn’t have to be brutal! FightCamp’s free at-home boxing workouts will have you loving your journey to your best summer body yet.
body_text: As summer comes careening around the corner, we’re eyeing our tank tops, cutoffs, and bathing suits with no small amount of trepidation. Listen, looking good has nothing to do with being in shape. But feeling strong, confident, and healthy sure does. And while winter temps and chilly weather can keep us cuddled up on the couch, getting that healthy tone in time for summer doesn’t have to be an arduous or impossible task. Boxing can be one of the best ways to get in shape in time for summer because it’s fun, requires very little to zero equipment, and you can do it anywhere, anytime. There’s sometimes a perception that to box, you need a boxing gym, a sparring partner, and boxing equipment. But shadowboxing without boxing gloves, hand wraps, or a punching bag can still be a workout that will have you sweating and wanting more. With boxing programs like FightCamp, you can easily incorporate calorie-burning boxing workouts from the convenience of your home, and tone your way to your summer body. The FightCamp app features many free workouts that can be done with or without boxing equipment. You can box in your living room, in your driveway, or even at the park with friends, since the app can be conveniently downloaded onto your phone or tablet. With consistent healthy choices, you can feel stronger and look leaner for summer. 5 Tips To Get In Summer Shape 1. Do The Workouts That Are Fun For You Nothing kills a fitness goal like a workout you hate doing. With the FightCamp app you have access to multiple styles of boxing workouts from traditional boxing to kickboxing in 4, 6, or 8-round increments. If you want to really hone in on one particular technique, you can! And if you prefer punches over kicks, you can find workouts designed with that focus. You’ll also find a whole range of body strength and core workouts that you can pick and choose to build your favorite workout on the app. 2. Find a Boxing Community Achieving any goal is easier when you have support and accountability, but achieving fitness goals is also more fun when you have those things. On the free FightCamp App, you can get your friends and family members hooked on boxing with you and spur each other on! Even better, you’ll become part of our online FightCamp Community , where you can trade stats, engage in friendly competition, and find motivation. 3. Eat Clean and Stay Hydrated Getting that summer tone requires a multi-prong approach. Choosing unprocessed foods, minimizing alcohol and sugar intake, and preparing lean meats and plant-based proteins will help further your fitness goals significantly. A boxer’s diet is not a fad diet. It’s about meal prep, healthy choices, and feeding your body enough of the right things. Keeping a water bottle always at your side during the day will make staying hydrated a habit that you don’t even have to think about anymore. 4. Get Enough Sleep and Recover We cannot overemphasize the importance of sleep and recovery when it comes to health and getting in shape. If you’re working out consistently, you need to let your body recharge and recover. That means 7-8 hours of sleep each night. Make sleep a priority and you’ll be ready to box your way to your best summer body! 5. Trust The Process Consistency, consistency, consistency! Results don’t happen overnight, but trust that your workouts and healthy habits are paying off. Even a 25-minute boxing session 3 or 4 days per week will help strengthen your muscles and tone your body. Small steps add up to big change. Work Hard, Big Rewards Your summer body is right around the corner. Let yourself enjoy the process of getting in shape and living your best life for the rest of your life. title: Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. Announces April 2022 Bitcoin Self-Mining, Hosting Co-location and Operational Update
summary: Mawson is pleased to announce Bitcoin self-mining, hosting co-location and operational updates for April 2022.
body_text: Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. Announces April 2022 Bitcoin Self-Mining, Hosting Co-location and Operational Update Mawson produced record 171 Self-Mined Bitcoin in April, +384% vs April 2021 Mawson Self-Mining and Hosting Co-location operating at approximately 2.4 Exahash as at end April, expected to rise to approximately 3.3 Exahash by end May 2022, +37.5% month on month Mawson now has over 36,000 ASIC Bitcoin Miners deployed at its facilities across the USA and Australia across its Self-Mining and Hosting Co-location businesses, +63% vs March 2022 Self-Mining expected to be operating at approximately 1.8 Exahash end of May, producing approximately 8.0 Bitcoin per day[1] 630 Bitcoin produced in FY 2022 to end of April Sydney , Australia and New York City, USA — May 12th, 2022 — Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. (NASDAQ:MIGI) (“Mawson”), a digital infrastructure provider, announces unaudited Bitcoin production and operational update for April 2022. Mawson Self-Mining and Hosting Co-location operating at approximately 2.4 Exahash as at end of April, expected to rise to approximately 3.3 Exahash by end of May 2022. Bitcoin Self-Mining Update: In April Mawson produced 171 Bitcoin, +384% vs April 2021 April average hash rate at approximately 1.3 Exahash, +583% vs April 2021 April end of month hash rate at approximately 1.4 Exahash, +679% vs April 2021 May end of month hash rate expected to be approximately 1.8 Exahash, producing approximately 8.0 Bitcoin per day[1] Hosting Co-location Update: Mawson Hosting Co-location at 28 megawatts online end of April (+75% vs March 2022), expected to rise to approximately 52 megawatts online by end of May (+85% vs April 2022), as Mawson customers Celsius Mining LLC (100 megawatts) and Foundry Digital LLC (12 megawatts) deployments are scaled up. Operational Update: In April Mawson continued to build out and expand its existing and new facilities in the USA and Australia. ASIC Bitcoin miners continue to be delivered on a monthly basis, with a batch of Canaan A1246 miners delivered during the month. April was characterized by a rise in network difficulty. Despite this, monthly Bitcoin production was up +1% vs March 2022, and up +384% vs April 2021. Mawson now has over 36,000 ASIC Bitcoin Miners deployed at its facilities across the USA and Australia across its Self-Mining and Hosting Co-location businesses, up from 22,000 in March 2022. Midland, Pennsylvania facility: Modular Data Centers (MDCs) now being rolled out progressively, site expected to have approximately 52 megawatts of mining hardware online by the end of May 2022. Sandersville, Georgia facility: 38 Modular Data Centers (MDCs) online, site now fully operational at approximately 80 megawatts. Stage 3 expansion approved to 230 megawatts (capable of accommodating up to 7.5 Exahash) with development planning for 150 megawatt expansion commencing in June 2022. New South Wales, Australia facility: Site commissioning ongoing, with operational ramp up expected to occur steadily throughout May and June, with approximately 0.1 Exahash online by the end of May. The facility is expected to be fully operational with approximately 0.4 EH online by June 2022. Expected Hash Rate Growth: Mawson expects Bitcoin Self-Mining to be at 4.0 EH by Q3, 2022, and target of 5.5 EH online by early Q1 2023 reiterated. Aerial view of Midland, Pennsylvania facility development (April 2022) USA Modular Data Center (MDC) fabrication facility Aerial view of Midland, Pennsylvania facility development (May 2022) James Manning, CEO and Founder of Mawson , said, “April was operationally solid for the business, with a particularly pleasing result in our hosting co-location business ramp up, where we expanded from 16 megawatts online in March, to 28 megawatts online in April. We expect this to rise to 52 megawatts online by the end of May, as we progressively roll out and expand our second major Bitcoin mining facility in the town of Midland, Pennsylvania. The Mawson team continued to expand over the month with more high-quality individuals joining the Mawson family. We anticipate a meaningful step up in our Bitcoin Self-Mining operations in May, to 1.8 Exahash, and expect further solid growth on this front in May and June.” About Mawson Infrastructure Mawson Infrastructure Group (NASDAQ: MIGI) is a digital infrastructure provider, with multiple operations throughout the USA and Australia. Mawson’s vertically integrated model is based on a long-term strategy to promote the global transition to the new digital economy. Mawson matches sustainable energy infrastructure with next-generation mobile data centre (MDC) solutions, enabling low-cost Bitcoin production and on-demand deployment of infrastructure assets. With a strong focus on shareholder returns and an aligned board and management, Mawson Infrastructure Group is emerging as a global leader in ESG focused Bitcoin mining and digital infrastructure.
